name: Remnants
description: A code editor built on the open VS Code source, with every AI feature taken out. For Windows, macOS and Linux.

hero.lede: A code editor built on the open VS Code source, with every AI feature taken out. Nothing asks you to sign in, and it sends no usage data.
hero.also: Also for Windows on ARM, macOS and Linux.
notes: The Windows installer is just for you and needs no admin rights.
If Windows says it protected your PC, click More info, then Run anyway.
hero.away: Remnants runs on Windows, macOS and Linux. Open this page on your computer to download it.

features.label: Layout
features.title: Views live in the status bar
body: The activity bar is hidden, so the editor gets the room. Explorer, Search, Source Control, Run and Debug and Extensions sit at the left of the status bar, the terminal and settings at the right.
The switch of the open view is lit.

main.name: f5
main.alt: Source Control opened from the status bar, with a commit message typed

features.label: Diff
features.title: See every change side by side
body: Click a changed file in Source Control and Remnants opens it next to the last commit. Removed text is marked on the left, added text on the right.

main.name: f1
main.alt: A side-by-side diff of format.js against the last commit

features.label: Terminal
features.title: Your shell, right under the code
body: The terminal opens in the panel below the editor and starts your shell in the project folder. <kbd>Ctrl+`</kbd> shows or hides it.

main.name: f2
main.alt: The terminal below the editor with nine tests passing

features.label: Search
features.title: Find text across the project
body: Search lists every match, grouped by file, with a count per file. <kbd>Ctrl+Shift+F</kbd> opens it, and a click on a match opens the file at that line.

main.name: f3
main.alt: Fourteen results in six files for parseDuration

features.label: Extensions
features.title: Extensions from Open VSX
body: The Extensions view searches and installs from Open VSX, the open registry for editor extensions. Your languages and themes work as you know them.

main.name: f4
main.alt: Four extensions installed from Open VSX

pair.label: Themes
pair.title: Light and dark, as you like
body: A light and a dark theme come with it, and any theme from Open VSX works too.

items: Search shows its results on the very first search.
The optional update check asks the Remnants download site for the latest release.
Report Issue and the license link open on the Remnants download site.
On an ARM PC, the x64 build's warning opens the ARM64 download.
The installers name Remnants as the publisher.

requirements: Windows 10 or later, x64 or ARM64
macOS 12 or later, Apple silicon or Intel
Linux with glibc 2.34 or newer, x64 or arm64
About 175 MB to download on Windows

privacy.title: No AI and no telemetry
body: The chat panel, agent sessions, voice features and the built-in AI extension were removed from the source. Telemetry and crash reports are off, and there is no sign-in.
Extension searches and updates go to Open VSX. The release check is off until you turn it on.

data.title: Settings stay when you update
body: Settings and keybindings live in %APPDATA%\Remnants on Windows, ~/Library/Application Support/Remnants on macOS and ~/.config/Remnants on Linux. Extensions live in ~/.remnants/extensions.

keys: Show or hide the side bar
keys_note: The usual shortcuts. On macOS, Cmd takes the place of Ctrl.

basics.title: Get started
steps: Double-click it and follow the setup.
Open a folder and start coding.

basics.title: Updates
body: Remnants never updates itself. Install the new release over the old one; settings and extensions stay. Turn on remnants.checkForUpdates to hear about new releases.

basics.title: Removing it
body: On Windows, uninstall it under Settings, Apps. On a Mac, move it to the Trash. On Linux, remove the package. Your settings folder stays until you delete it.

a: Yes. It is free and open source under the MIT License, with no account.

faq.q: Why does Windows say it protected my PC?
a: Remnants is not signed with a paid certificate, so Windows asks once. Click More info, then Run anyway. Every download has a checksum in the checksum file.

faq.q: Does it have any AI features?
a: No. They were removed from the source, not just switched off, and telemetry is off too.

faq.q: Which files are there for macOS and Linux?
a: macOS: a disk image for Apple silicon and for Intel.
Linux: a .deb for Debian and Ubuntu, an .rpm for Fedora and openSUSE, a tarball for any distribution, and a PKGBUILD for Arch.

faq.q: Where are my settings and extensions?
a: Settings live in %APPDATA%\Remnants on Windows, ~/Library/Application Support/Remnants on macOS and ~/.config/Remnants on Linux. Extensions live in ~/.remnants/extensions. Uninstalling leaves both in place.
